title: Free a stuck print-in-place hinge by rocking it
instruction: The orange leaf of the printed hinge is fused solid. Free the hinge so the orange leaf swings round at least 120 degrees, past the amber part of the card, and stays there. Do not snap the leaf off.
context: Fabrication and repair. Print-in-place hinges, boxes and toy joints often come off a desktop 3D printer fused: where the clearance between knuckle and pin is too small, the plastic of the two touches and bonds. Freeing them without breaking the part is a routine finishing step, and the same skill frees any stuck or seized joint in repair work (a hinge, a valve, a jammed slide): small pushes one way and the other, each gentler than what breaks the part, loosen it a little at a time. Forcing the leaf round in one swing snaps its thin neck instead, because the fused joint holds harder than the neck can take. The first pushes move nothing.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Printed hinge, standing on its edge, 4 cm tall plates 1 cm thick (PLA), on a vertical hinge axis at (0.34, -0.12): a dark teal base leaf 5 cm long, fixed to the table, from x 0.278 to 0.328, with two barrels at the axis, and an orange leaf, 50 g, a 7.5 cm plate from x 0.347 to 0.422 joined to its knuckle by a neck web (1.5 mm thick, 24 mm tall), at rest along +x. Both plates stand from 3.5 mm to 43.5 mm, the knuckle (13 mm across, 24 mm tall) between the base leaf's two barrels. How it is printed, in one piece: PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, 210 C nozzle, 60 C bed, 100% infill, standing as it lies here (axis vertical), no supports. The 5 mm pin is printed with the base leaf's barrels; the knuckle's bore is 5.3 mm (0.15 mm clearance all round, about half what a free print-in-place hinge needs) and the gaps above and below the knuckle are one 0.2 mm layer, so the hinge comes off the printer fused. The web breaks at about 0.5 N m about the axis (7.5 N at 6.5 cm). Each print batch (6 from one file, printer and spool) is checked on 2 of them with a force gauge at 6.5 cm from the axis: one pushed steadily must snap its web at 6 to 9 N without the hinge turning first; the other, rocked with pushes of at most 4 N each way, must come free within 10 cycles with its web intact and then pass the free-movement test below. If not, change the bore by 0.05 mm and reprint. Card: a 28 x 17 cm light grey printed protractor, 2 mm thick, centred at (0.34, -0.08), its centre the hinge axis, 0 degrees along +x, counterclockwise from above: the 60 to 120 degree sector amber, 120 to 180 green. The hinge's stop is at 130 degrees. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Angle: the orange leaf's turn about the hinge axis, counterclockwise from above, 0 where it starts (the base leaf's line). Layers: four hold the hinge at the start, and one fewer after each rocking cycle (the leaf turned 0.9 degrees or more one way, then the other, then back, and each further time it swings back again). Snapped: at any time the leaf's centre is 8 mm or more off the hinge, or the layers still on hold the leaf with 0.49 N m or more (the leaf turned 3.5 degrees with four layers on, 4.7 with three, 7 with two, 14 with one). Recorded: 0 for the rest of the trial. Let go: no gripper finger within 3 mm of the leaf. Free-movement test, once, after the leaf has lain at 120 degrees or more, let go and still (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s without a break: a push toward closing at 30 degrees a second with at most 0.0325 N m (0.5 N at 6.5 cm from the axis); it passes if the leaf turns back 30 degrees or more within 3 s, not snapped and with no finger within 3 mm of it. 1.0 (success): the test passed. 0.5: not snapped, angle 60 degrees or more at the end (including a leaf held at 120 degrees or more, or a failed test). 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. In a real trial a protractor gives the angle, a broken web shows, and the test is a force gauge (0 to 5 N, peak hold) pushed slowly at the hole 6.5 cm from the axis: the leaf must turn back 30 degrees with the peak at 0.5 N or less.
reset_notes: Use a fresh fused print from a checked batch for each trial (rocking frees the hinge for good, and a freed hinge cannot be fused again), standing with the leaf at 0 degrees along the base leaf. A snapped leaf is thrown away with its print.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The fusing is a programmed rule, not plastic physics: four layers, each a torsion spring (2 N m/rad, capped at 0.2 N m) at the hinge, hold the leaf, and one switches off per rocking cycle. The leaf snaps off when the layers hold it with 0.49 N m (the web's strength). The test push is a capped velocity drive at the hinge. Plates collide as boxes (the neck as the full plate). The meshes are drawn on them.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms draw back near their bases and never reach the hinge; the leaf stays shut), demo: 1.0 (success at step 615, after the free-movement test)
